history.alt_text: A mechanical stopwatch resting on a stack of regulatory documents on a plain desk
history.caption: Enterprises face overlapping incident-reporting clocks that demand action in hours, not days.
history.title: AI-Incident-Clock-Flatlay

style_when: the story is regulatory or contractual — a filing, a mandate, a rate notice, a certificate, a purchase order that changed the economics
prompt: Overhead flat-lay photograph, top-down 90-degree view, 50mm lens with a razor-sharp focal plane. A sleek, modern mechanical stopwatch resting on top of a stack of muted, heavy paper regulatory rulebooks and embossed filings. Extreme asymmetry, placing the documents and stopwatch in the bottom left corner with generous empty desk space to the right. Even diffused daylight, soft contact shadows, matte paper tones, tactile paper stock, dark wood desk surface, refined editorial aesthetic. No legible text.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random letters, numbers, UI, watermarks, typography, legible writing
rationale: The story revolves around competing regulatory mandates and filing deadlines. A document flatlay captures the bureaucratic reality of these distinct rulebooks and the stark contrast between active and delayed timelines.
subject: a mechanical stopwatch resting on open regulatory rulebooks
core_thesis: Enterprises are relying on the AI Act's 15-day incident reporting deadline, but their actual regulatory clock is driven by existing rules that demand action in as little as four hours.
core_conflict: Delayed 15-day vendor compliance vs. immediate 4-hour enterprise regulatory reality
alt_text: The 4-Hour AI Deadline. A mechanical stopwatch resting on a stack of regulatory documents on a plain desk
caption: The 4-Hour AI Deadline: The real deadline for enterprise AI incidents is 4 hours.
title: The 4-Hour AI Deadline
